svg.title: Relay Velvet wiring reference
svg.desc: Base-harness wiring reference with Alnico II bridge and neck humbuckers, a Retrotron Nashville middle pickup, a standard five-way contact map, an unused tone push-pull, rear-view A500K volume and tone pots, five operating states, and common ground.

g.text: BASE HARNESS • MATCH IDENTICAL BOXED NET LABELS • FUNCTIONAL SWITCH CONTACTS MUST BE METERED
Use supplied lead guides and a meter; labels show electrical roles, not wire colors
BRIDGE • GFS Pro Series Alnico II
NECK • GFS Pro Series Alnico II
Functional contact map • verify by continuity
Rows are the blade throws; columns are the five positions. Adjacent throws overlap in positions 2 and 4.
One pole supplies BUS. The second pole of the standard five-way is unused.
Functional contact map • verify by continuity
The tone pot works as a standard tone control.
Its push-pull switch is reserved for a future focus contour.
Leave all six switch lugs unconnected and insulated.
The switch position has no effect on the sound.
No treble bleed in this revision.
REAR VIEW • shaft away • lugs down
Fed from BUS, the volume input.
REAR VIEW • shaft away • lugs down
GND = pickup returns + separate shields/cases • volume CCW lug • 22 nF tone return • output jack sleeve.
Both pot cases, conductive switch chassis, cavity shielding, and bridge/string ground are bonded to the same ground network.
Humbuckers stay in full series: insulate a single split lead, or join and insulate two separate series ends per the pickup guide.
Meter the five selector positions, confirm BUS reaches only the selected pickups, then tap-test all five positions.
The Nashville must sound alone in position 3 and blend only in positions 2 and 4.
